To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

metamorphic degassing of CO 2 from sedimentary basin rocks is unlikely to be a major source of atmospheric CO 2 during metamorphic episodes, and that the permeability of the sedimentary basin is an important control on the amount of CO 2 that can be transported from metamorphic aureoles to the atmosphere.
the metamorphic CO2 degassing from the Franklin large igneous province is constrained by numerical modeling of metamorphic reactions and fluid flow.

the metamorphic aureoles of mafic sills in carbonate rocks of the Shaler Group in the Minto Block of Victoria Island, Arctic Canada, are consistent with a host-rock permeability of about 10 −17 to 10 −18 m 2.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the large igneous event (LIE) of the Franklinian mobile belt (FMB) in the evolution of the Neoprotozoic (NPP) Earth's climate.
the role of CO 2 degassing from the mantle in driving climate change.
the origin of the Franklin magmatism, which occurred at ca. 720Ma, during the breakup of the Rodinia Supercontinent and the subsequent glaciation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the CO 2 degassing from the metamorphic aureoles during the 600-yr period of the Franklin magmatism would be only a small fraction of the 8 ppm (weight) of CO 2 that is estimated to be required to trigger the Sturtian glaciations.

the metamorphic degassing of the Minto Inliers did not contribute to the CO 2 -rich greenhouse climate of the Neoprotozoic, but it did contribute to a more moderate CO 2 climate, which was conducive to the evolution of life.
the metamorphic aureoles of the sills were too small to have been the main source of the atmospheric CO 2 during the Sturtian glaciations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the Franklin large igneous province is not a significant contributor to the CO 2 budget of the Neopro-terozoic atmosphere, but the host-rock permeability is a significant constraint on this conclusion.
metamorphic degassing of CO2 is unlikely to have been a significant source of CO2 to the atmosphere during the Neoprotozoic Franklin large ignious event.
the CO 2 degassing of the Franklin magmatism was not significant enough to cause a significant change to the global carbon cycle.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the metamorphic degassing of CO2 during the formation of contact aureoles is not a viable explanation for the large amount of CO2 that is required to explain the Neoproterzoic glaciation.
metamorphic reactions and associated degassing are not the only source of carbonic gases to the atmosphere.
metamorphism in sedimentary basins does not necessarily result in large-scale degassing of metamorphogenic CO 2.
